subject: On-prem / air-gapped deployment follow-up: hardware & offline ops
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <t.ellis@legacybank.com>, Priya Suresh <priya.suresh@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: on-prem air-gapped qualification

Hi Tom and Priya,

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone has the same notes and next steps. High-level requirements we heard: 

- Deployment mode: private on-prem, fully air-gapped (no outbound traffic allowed from inference nodes).
- Pilot profile: start small for a POC (inference for document ingestion + chat assist) with ramp to production over Q3/Q4.
- Hardware constraints: you mentioned existing rack space but uncertain on GPU availability and procurement timeline.
- Upgrades/ops: upgrades must be scheduled outside business hours and performed by your on-prem ops team; you asked about how Redwood delivers signed upgrades and offline install artifacts.
- Security/compliance: you will need a signed MSA and an SOC2 evidence package for procurement.

Open questions for you:
1) Can you confirm rack units available and current GPU models in the target rack (model and memory)?
2) Any strict kernel/OS versions we need to support or a pre-approved image list?
3) Who on your side will own performing offline installs and weekend upgrades (name + contact)?
4) Timeline for procurement if you want to start a 2-node pilot?

Attachments: I am including an initial on-prem hardware spec and a network airgap checklist for your infra team to review.

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep-dive with our infra/solutions team next week to review the checklist and finalize hardware minimums. I propose Tue 2027-04-13 at 10:00 AM PT.
- We will share an encrypted offline image delivery plan and a draft MSA for procurement.

If those times work, I can send a calendar invite with Dev and Neha included.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

- Current hardware in the target rack: 4x NVIDIA A100 80GB across two chassis (we can allocate 2 GPUs per chassis). We do not have H100s yet.
- Procurement: lead time for additional GPUs is 8-12 weeks. For the pilot we would likely reuse existing A100 gear and allocate two nodes.
- Airgap policy: outbound traffic from inference nodes is blocked. We can provision a temporary jumpbox with controlled egress for initial bootstrap if needed, but overall the nodes cannot reach the internet.
- Upgrades: must be scheduled on weekends. We will have an on-call ops engineer perform installs; Priya will be the primary contact (priya.suresh@legacybank.com).

1) What are the minimum GPU / node counts you recommend for a 2-node pilot to achieve acceptable latency for our use case?

Thanks Tom  great context. Answers inline below plus next steps.

1) Minimum for a 2-node pilot: we typically recommend at least 2x A100 80GB (one GPU per inference service process) or 2x H100 80GB if you have them. With 2x A100 80GB we can run a small production-like pilot for document-level retrieval + chat with conservative batching. Expected median latency will depend on request sizes but is usually in the 150-300ms range for short prompts.

2) Offline artifacts: yes  Redwood provides signed/offline install bundles and a checksum manifest. We can deliver via encrypted USB or an air-gapped transfer bundle. We will also provide a runbook and signed checksums.

3) Storage/RAM: recommended starting point per node is 8TB NVMe for model shards and replay, and 512GB RAM for KV cache headroom. If you plan to host multiple large models concurrently you should size higher.

Operational notes: 
- Upgrades are shipped as signed artifacts. Our solutions team will coordinate with your on-call operator to perform weekend installs.
- We will prepare a staging image and an install checklist that your team can validate in a fenced staging environment before production cutover.

Attachments: onprem-hardware-specs.pdf (detailed CPU/RAM/IO recommendations) and the network-airgap-checklist.xlsx we shared earlier.

Proposed tech deep-dive: Tue 2027-04-13 10:00 AM PT with Dev and Neha. Please confirm and I will send an invite.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: on-prem air-gapped qualification (technical notes)

Hi Tom, quick technical follow-up from our side with specifics your ops team will find useful.

Hardware (per node, recommended minimum for POC):
- GPUs: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (supported) or 1x H100 80GB (preferred if available)
- CPU: 32 vCPU (AMD EPYC / Intel Xeon class)
- Memory: 512GB RAM
- Storage: 2x 4TB NVMe in RAID1 for model shards + 1x 8TB NVMe local for caches/workspace (we recommend fast NVMe for kv cache)
- Network: 25Gb internal fabric between nodes; isolated management network for the jumpbox

OS and drivers:
- Linux distro: RHEL 8.6, Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (we can support others but please list in advance)
- NVIDIA driver: 525.x or 535.x depending on GPU; we will confirm exact required driver in the tech call

Air-gapped install process (high level):
1) We provide a signed install bundle + checksum manifest.
2) Your operator stages the bundle on the jumpbox and performs a transplant to target nodes via a secured offline transfer.
3) Install verifies signed checksums, loads drivers and runtime artifacts, and performs a smoke test.
4) Redwood provides a verification script and runbook for the post-install validation.

Upgrades and rollbacks:
- Upgrades are applied as signed delta artifacts. We coordinate with your ops engineer and perform a staged rollout to one node at a time.
- Rollback runbooks are provided and tested in staging.

Action items for your ops team before the technical deep-dive:
- Confirm jumpbox capacity and whether temporary egress is permissible during install windows.
- Share exact kernel/OS versions and current driver versions.
- Share procurement ETA for additional GPUs if you decide to expand beyond the pilot.

Happy to walk through the install playbook on the call and to map exact driver bundles to your hardware.

Regards,
Dev Patel
